Senses.Explanation: Literally, to take hands and walk together. The phrase occurs 207 times in 105 allowlisted texts. Chan records use it as a verdict of admitted company: a speaker says that whoever can inspect his statement may walk hand in hand south of Mount Sumeru, that one who can seize the snake safely may walk with the old monk, or that one commentator walks with Nanquan. Its companions range from buddhas and patriarchs to named masters and interlocutors who meet the stated test. Yuanwu's case commentary joins the phrase to entering mud and water together, living and dying together, making close participation in a public case—not generic companionship—the phrase's characteristic Chan deployment.
Senses.Note: No distinct referent emerged: literal hand-taking supplies one recurrent metaphorical predicate, applied to different companions. Those companions are deployment variants, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若點檢得出，須彌南畔把手共行；若點檢不出，布袋裏老鴉雖活如死。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 列祖提綱錄 explicitly introduces Chan Master Jianfu Ben's hall address. Jianfu Ben is the exact speaker who says that anyone able to examine his statement may walk hand in hand south of Mount Sumeru.

Occurrences.Kwic: 與他把手共行。他從來有放行手段。敢與爾入泥入水。同死同生。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin says Xuedou's verse goes hand in hand with the case, expanding the image as entering mud and water and living and dying together; this is Yuanwu's commentary on Xuedou Chongxian.

Occurrences.Kwic: 於他七寸上。一揑揑住。便與老僧把手共行。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin explicitly quotes his former teacher Wuzu Fayan, who says that one able to seize the snake at seven inches may walk hand in hand with this old monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雪竇與南泉把手共行。一句說了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Yuanwu Keqin says Xuedou Chongxian goes hand in hand with Nanquan Puyuan and settles it in one phrase; Xuedou and Nanquan are the two grammatically named co-actors.
